dedupe_keys.name: tailings dam resilience through design and responsible management a case study ancold 2022

description: A conference paper on the resilience of an active coal tailings dam in New South Wales. The ANCOLD product page says the 2022 paper by Black, Kingsland and Russell of WSP describes an active coal tailings dam at an underground mine near Lake Macquarie with a capacity of 5,316 ML and a High A consequence category, built from 2006; weather events from 2007 to 2011 led to water building up in the dam, and sinkholes formed from old shallow workings, yet the dam was found to be robust with good management. The paper is not a free download: it costs 15 Australian dollars. Coverage is one dam. Caveats: only the abstract was read, and the licence is not stated on the page read. For simulation it is a real record of how rainfall and ground subsidence stress a tailings dam, to test failure and response scenarios. A related catalogue record is the Ballarat Gold Mine climate risk case study.
